title: burgee benchmark results
description: One run of `npm run bench`, for one suite. Written to benchmarks/results/<suite>/<YYYY-MM-DD>.json, which is where scripts/control-bands.ts reads its observations from.

commit.description: The commit the numbers describe, or `unknown` outside a checkout — never a guess.

machine.description: B2's milliseconds are a property of this machine as much as of the code, which is why the banded perf number is a ratio and not a duration.

axes.description: Per axis: measured, skipped (asked for, could not run) or not-run (not selected). Anything but `measured` carries a reason, and contributes no band value and no claim verdict.

method.description: How the numbers were produced, in prose, so the table can be read without the source.

records.description: Every measurement, in the one shape all four axes emit (B5).

variant.description: What was measured: a CLI variant, a host, an entry point, or a ratio of two of those, written `a ÷ b`.

samples.description: For a deterministic measurement (a byte count, a pass rate) this is 1 and median equals p95: a p95 over one sample is that sample, stated rather than hidden.

median.description: The gated and banded statistic. Never the p95: a tail-driven gate is what red-lit two unrelated PRs in issue #27.

gate.description: A deterministic per-PR bound. `why` is mandatory: a bound nobody can argue with is a bound nobody will maintain.

detail.description: Whatever reproducing the number needs: resolved paths, versions, raw counts.

bands.description: What Stage 6 reads. `scripts/control-bands.ts` picks `bands.<id>.value`. An entry with no value carries the status and reason instead — it is never zero, and never absent.

from.description: The record the value was read out of. A value with no `from` is refused by benchmarks/emit.ts.

claims.description: Every number the repository states in public, settled against a record. `met: false` and `status: "unmeasured"` are different outcomes and never collapse into each other.

source.description: The file that states it, so a reader can go and correct it.

$comment: "Turns" means `num_turns` as `claude -p --output-format json` reports it. Tokens are input + cache-creation + cache-read + output, as the same JSON reports them: leaving cache reads out would make a cached run look free, and a benchmark that rewards caching measures the cache.
